name: goosenecks
title: Goosenecks of the San Juan River, Utah, USA
note: The San Juan River entrenched about 300 m into flat-lying layered rock, looping back on itself below Goosenecks State Park: some 10 km of river for 2.4 km of westward progress, the canyon walls stepped in ledges and slopes.
grid: local azimuthal equidistant (sphere R=6371008.8 m) centred on centre_lat/centre_lon; x east, y north; row 0 = north edge; pixel centre x = (col + 0.5 - cols/2) * pixel_size_m, y = (rows/2 - row - 0.5) * pixel_size_m

source.dataset: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP), best-available DEM (3DEPElevation ImageServer)
source.native_resolution_m: 1 m lidar where the projects in lidar_1m_products_here cover the tile, elsewhere 1/3 arc-second (~10 m)
source.attribution: Courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey, 3D Elevation Program (3DEP)
source.resampling: Gaussian low-pass (sigma 0.90 source px) then bilinear

attribution: Courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey, 3D Elevation Program (3DEP)
encoding: 16-bit greyscale PNG: height_m = height_min_m + v / 65535 * (height_max_m - height_min_m)
